Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix into your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. Democrats are preparing to take power in Congress next year.
The party is united around the goal of expanding health coverage, but lawmakers disagree about how to do it.
NPR's Sam Greenglass reports.
The first step, says the next likely House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries, is to reverse Republican cuts to Medicaid and restore enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies.
But we also know, as Democrats, that a return to the status quo is not acceptable.
Jeffries said this month he backs lowering the eligibility age for Medicare, expanding it to cover vision, dental and hearing, and guaranteeing universal coverage for children.
Some Democrats are unsure. Others say reform needs to go further and want to advance single-payer insurance or Medicare for all.
Because President Trump may be unwilling to sign any of this, debates now over health care could shape the direction Democrats go in the 2028 presidential campaign.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Washington.
Health officials in Vermont say they've confirmed more than a dozen reports of measles.
Lola DeFore of Vermont Public says these are the first cases in the state in decades.
Until recently, measles cases were extraordinarily rare in Vermont, but Vermont state epidemiologist Emily Masaita says with vaccination rates declining and the virus making a comeback nationally, things were bound to change.
I think it shows that we are in such a different place than we were, you know, 15 years ago, 20 years ago.
The confirmed cases all involve members of connected households who weren't vaccinated against measles and had recently traveled to another state with an outbreak.
Health officials are urging all Vermonters to check their vaccination status.
For NPR News, I'm Lola DeFore in Montpelier.
Net migration into the United Kingdom has dropped to an almost 30-year low. Concern about immigration had prompted many people to vote for Brexit and has field support for far-right politicians.
NPR's Lauren Frere reports from London.
Government figures show fewer people from outside Europe migrating into the U.K., as well as asylum requests dropping by a third over the past year ending in September.
Overall, net migration has dropped to its lowest level since 1997, excluding the pandemic, down about 90 percent from 2023.
This could weaken support for far-right lawmaker Nigel Farage's anti-immigrant party, which has already been slumping in the polls amid corruption allegations.
Successive British governments on both the right and left have tightened immigration rules for workers and students and restricted the ways people can claim asylum.
But reduced immigration could potentially hinder the British economy by shrinking the workforce and straining public finances.
Lauren Frere, NPR News, London.
This is NPR.
Black Friday is expected to be the busiest shopping day of the Thanksgiving weekend.
A National Retail Federation survey finds about 126 million people plan to shop tomorrow.
Overall, slightly fewer people plan to shop between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday than last year, as some big retailer started offering deals weeks ago.
Cyber Monday is forecast to bring in the most online sales at more than 15 billion dollars.
Seabirds treat fishing vessels like a maritime buffet, but approaching a fishing rig can snag birds and kill them.
That's a risk that may be underestimated, according to seabirds who were employed to do some eavesdropping.
NPR's R.A. Daniel explains.
Jonathan Rutter, a marine biologist at the University of Oxford, worked with his colleagues to attach tiny audio recorders to four shearwater seabirds off of Spain,
a westland petrol in New Zealand, and seven northern gannets in the Celtic Sea.
Listening later, they heard this.
Boat noise.
It turned out that numerous boats showed up in the audio that didn't match public vessel tracks.
It's showing the extent of what we're not seeing.
Rutter isn't advocating for seabirds to be used as a surveillance or law enforcement tool,
but this technique reveals that the risk of seabird bycatch may be considerably higher than previously thought.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
Wall Street is closed for the Thanksgiving holiday trading resumes tomorrow. This is NPR.
This message comes from VCU.
At Virginia Commonwealth University, research is knowledge put to work.
Ranked among the nation's top 50 public research universities, VCU is expanding what's known and what's possible.

Vermont confirms more than a dozen measles cases, its first in decades, linked to unvaccinated households
UK net migration drops to lowest level since 1997, weakening Nigel Farage's anti-immigrant party
National Retail Federation expects 126 million Americans to shop on Black Friday, slightly fewer than last year
Researchers use audio recorders on seabirds to reveal unreported fishing boat activity and bycatch risk
